newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Gunmen kill six civilians on Liberian highway.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill six civilians on Liberian highway.

text.p: Suspected Liberian militia killed six civilians and wounded two when they ambushed a bush taxi on a highway on Saturday, peacekeeping officials said.

West African peacekeepers policing the highway between the capital Monrovia and the western town of Tubmanburg said the victims were all believed to be local traders who commute between Monrovia and the interior.
"They (gunmen) fled into the bush after killing the civilians. And they made away with money and valuables belonging to the victims," said a Nigerian peacekeeping soldier.

It was the first major incident in the war-ravaged country since troops of the ECOMOG West African peackeeping force stationed in Liberia since 1990 began taking away weapons from militiamen on November 22.
Diasarmament is the most important part of a peace process to end nearly seven years of civil war and bring back democracy to the republic founded by freed American slaves in 1847.

A faction of the ULIMO militia at the centre of clashes in the region accused a rival wing for the attack. Fighting has flared in the area despite an August 20 ceasefire committing warring parties to a new pact after failure of earlier accords.
"We are blaming ULIMO-K for the ambush because they control the area and they even fled with the taxi cab in which the passengers were," said Solomon Saydee of the rival ULIMO-J.
Voluntary disarmament is scheduled to end on January 31 after which ECOMOG says it was likely to resort to force to retrieve weapons from recalcitrant armed rebels.
More than 400 combatants have been disarmed and demobilised in the exercise which is expected to clear the way for presidential elections planned by next May.
About 60,000 combatants, 15,000 of them child-fighters are to be demobilised, but officials said only 1,500 child-soldiers had handed over their weapons so far.
The war has killed more than 150,000 people and displaced more than half the population of more than 2.5 million people.
